issues.legal_issue: Agricultural produce does not become taxable income merely upon its production or receipt; income arises when the produce is disposed of by sale, consumption, or business use.
material_facts: The taxpayer owned a cardamom plantation and sold cardamom during the accounting year.
The taxpayer claimed that the cardamom sold was accumulated produce received in earlier years.
The tax authorities rejected that explanation for lack of reliable supporting evidence.
issues.conclusion: The produce’s receipt in earlier years did not exempt income derived from its sale in the accounting year; agricultural income arose upon its disposal by sale or qualifying use.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 3 read with section 4 and the definition of agricultural income in the Madras Plantations Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1955, the charge is on income, not mere production or receipt of a commodity. Income ordinarily arises when the commodity is disposed of by sale, consumption, or use in the assessee’s business for the assessee’s benefit. Dooars Tea Co. Ltd. v. Commissioner of Agricultural Income-tax, West Bengal, [1962] 3 S.C.R. 157, establishes that sale is not necessary where agricultural produce is used in the assessee’s business; it does not establish that income arises merely upon receipt of the produce. State of Kerala v. Bhavani Tea Produce Co. Ltd., [1966] 2 S.C.R. 92, concerned statutory delivery that transferred ownership and does not establish accrual before disposal, use, or sale.

predicates.agricultural_income_tax_case: The proceeding concerns whether income from agricultural produce is taxable under an agricultural income tax regime.
predicates.produce_received_before_accounting_year: The produce at issue was received before the accounting year in which its income is assessed.
predicates.produce_disposed_by_sale_or_business_use: The taxpayer sold the produce or consumed or used it in the taxpayer’s business during the accounting year.

issues.definition: When a produce-related agricultural income tax case involves produce received earlier but disposed of by sale or business use during the accounting year, income arises in the year of that disposal.

issues.legal_issue: An earlier application to compound agricultural income tax does not by itself establish that produce sold in a later accounting year was taxed in the earlier years.
material_facts: The taxpayer had applied to compound tax for earlier years and paid tax determined under the compounding provisions.
The taxpayer contended that the cardamom sold in the accounting year had already been taxed in those earlier years.
There was no evidence that the crop sold related to the years for which the taxpayer had applied to compound tax.
issues.conclusion: The taxpayer’s contention that the produce sold in the accounting year had already suffered tax in earlier years could not be accepted without evidence linking that crop to those years.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 65 of the Madras Plantations Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1955, an application to compound tax and payment of the tax so determined do not alone prove that particular produce sold later was produced in, or taxed for, the earlier years. Evidence must establish that the crop sold related to the years for which compounding was sought.

predicates.prior_year_compounding_application: The taxpayer applied to compound tax for earlier years.
predicates.produce_sold_in_accounting_year: The taxpayer sold agricultural produce during the accounting year under assessment.
predicates.evidence_links_produce_to_compounded_yea: Evidence establishes that the produce sold in the accounting year came from years for which the taxpayer applied to compound tax.

issues.definition: When a taxpayer has sought compounding for earlier years but sells produce in the accounting year without evidence linking that produce to the compounded years, earlier taxation of the sold produce is not established.
